title: Outcome synopsis + weekly digest
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable snapshot of what I actually shipped / learned this week and the tiny commitments I can hold to move target outcomes forward. Treat as a rolling digest — one entry per week + micro-retrospective.

How I use this doc:
- Fill the top summary each Friday (or Monday if Friday slips).
- Capture one experiment and one blockage.
- 1–2 micro-actions for next week (timeboxed).
- If an item looks like a pattern (recurring blocker or growth signal), draft a short RFC and move to proper project tracking.

WEEK 2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-16 (baseline week)
Summary: Focused on trimming dialog latency for the small-batch route; landed a change that reduces tail latency by ~12% for requests under 512 tokens. Felt productive but context-switching with feature requests slowed follow-ups.
Outcome signals:
- Latency (p50/p95) for small-batch route: p50 down 6%, p95 down 12% (from internal dashboard).
- Deploy velocity: 2 incremental deploys (canary -> prod), 1 rollback flagged by SRE (fast rollback tested).
- Personal energy: 3/5 (fragmented afternoons).
Experiment: Introduced a lightweight KV cache check-before-batch for prefix hits. Preliminary: +7% token cost reduction for synthetic perf tests.
Blocker: Manual rollbacks still take too long (context: ops runbook ambiguous on step 3).
Micro-actions next week:
- Draft explicit rollback script and share with SRE for feedback (30m).
- Reserve 90 minutes blocked calendar on Tue for 2 uninterrupted feature reviews.

WEEK 2025-02-17 -> 2025-02-23
Summary: Script draft done; SRE had quick edits; merged. Spent time writing up small reproducible benchmark (Jupyter) for cache experiment. Still under-powered on quality evals — need human review set.
Outcome signals:
- Cache experiment validated in staging: consistent 5–8% cost reduction; slightly higher hallucination risk in edge prompt set (needs eval).
- Review throughput: 6 PRs reviewed, 3 approved.

Experiment: A/B prompt pairs to stress test hallucination with cached prefix.
Blocker: No dedicated eval reviewers — QA bandwidth low.
Micro-actions:
- Put up a short ask in #model-evals for 2 reviewers for one-off session (20m).
- Create a 10-min rubric for the prompt pairs so reviewers have focused task.

REFLECTION (rolling):
- Signal vs noise: focusing on p95 improvements feels measurable and motivating; but quality regressions show up late. Need to bake small evals earlier in the flow.
- Commitments are more reliable when small and timeboxed.

Quarterly outcome draft (working):
Objective: Reduce serving unit cost and maintain output fidelity for customer-facing chat flows.
Proposed outcome signals (not final):
- KR1: Reduce average token cost per session by 18% (by 2025-06-30).
- KR2: Keep human-evaluated quality degradation <= 2 percentage points on core prompt set.
- KR3: Cut median inference latency for 0–512 token sessions by 10%.
Notes: KR1 and KR2 trade off — need explicit guardrails and small-sample evals on any cost-saving patch. KR3 should be achievable through batching + kernel selection optimizations.

Personal habits / cadence I want to maintain:
- 90-min deep block twice a week (no meetings) for main project work.
- Friday 30-min digest: quick update to this doc + add 1 lesson learned.
- Weekly 10-min pairing with a reviewer (rotate) to speed feedback loops.

Unresolved questions / things to test:
- What minimal eval size correlates with human review pass rate? (5 prompts? 20?)
- Can we automate an early-warning classifier for hallucination spikes tied to cache hits? (prototype idea: small classifier over model logits + prefix-similarity)
- Do we need a separate perf-only merge window to avoid last-minute regressions?

Quick checklist (today):
- [x] Finish rollback script PR + follow-up with SRE.
- [x] Add short benchmarking notebook to repo (bench/kv-cache.ipynb).
- [ ] Draft the 10-min rubric and post in #model-evals.
- [ ] Schedule a 90-min focus block on Tue.

Notes-to-self snippets (untidy):
- Avoid rewriting tests right before canary — flaky window.
- If p95 regressions observed, triage with 2-step: (1) check kernel selection diff, (2) check batching distribution shift.
- Keep prompts for human eval minimal: context + 2 shots + 1 follow-up.

Links and quick refs:
- Benchmark notebook: github.com/redwood/infra/bench/kv-cache (PR: #1342).
- Rollback runbook (draft): CONFLUENCE:ROLLBACK-2025-02 (see step 3 note).
- Slack thread on cache tradeoffs: slack://channel/infra/thread-7211

If I only do one thing next week: get the rubric in front of a reviewer and run a 20-sample eval. That will either greenlight the cache change or surface edge cases early.

End of digest entry.

-- Maya

(Last quick thought) Keep entries concise — future-me should be able to scan months and see pattern shifts. If something looks like a new project, promote to proper project ticket + add cross-team collaborator list.
